review_notes:
I read the whole file and grepped for uses of `equivExterior` and `associated_neg_proof`. I did not read the definition files for the Clifford algebra, so I did not check whether its `CommRing`/`AddCommGroup` assumptions could be weakened. The contraction lemmas and the `changeForm` lemmas are already stated over a general `CommRing R`, with arbitrary `Q`, `Q'`, `Q''`, `B` and `B'`. Their hypotheses are only the ones the proofs need.

The one specialised statement is `equivExterior`, which assumes `[Invertible (2 : R)]`. Its docstring says it holds more generally when `Q` is divisible by two. The general form is already available as `changeFormEquiv h` for any `B` with `B.toQuadraticMap = 0 - Q`. A weaker-hypothesis `equivExterior` would be an explicit-hypothesis variant of `changeFormEquiv`, so I do not count it as a defect. The `Nontrivial` instance would not generalise without new mathematics. I found no concrete, well-supported generalisation, so I report none.
